column1: # swarm manifest — single source of truth for what a `cpo` swarm contains.
# Consumed by swarm-init.sh, swarm-sync.sh, and swarm-onboard.sh via
# manifest_walk in swarm-lib.sh, so first-stamp, upgrade, and onboard cannot
# diverge. Add a new artifact in ONE place: here.
# Per-type dispatch: at apply time, swarm_type_of() resolves a repo's archetype
# from its .claude/swarm-type marker; for a cpo swarm the marker is 'cpo' and
# this file is the consumed manifest.
#   - lines starting with '#' and blank lines are ignored
#   - fields are pipe-delimited, leading/trailing whitespace per field is trimmed
#   - target-path is relative to the target repo
#     (except gitignore, where this field is .gitignore itself; the
#     template-path is the line we ensure is present in it)
#   - The cpo swarm directory IS the operator's product-vision repo. Doctrine
#     and product-template/) is refreshed centrally. Operator-owned content
#     (products/, stress-test-log/) is seeded once and never touched by sync
#   - The permission-gate ALLOWS git push (the cpo's function is pushing its
#     own vision repo so the operator can read it). This diverges from
#     engineering-cto, which denies push. Both compose against the same
#   - No TEAM_LEAD, no PROJECT_SPEC/ADR, no test-gate / docs-check /
#     dod-affirm, no pre-commit hook, no test-cmd — the cpo is a single
#     conversational agent, not a team-of-engineers building software.
